key_insight: At 12.5% La substitution in BaTiO3, enhanced electronic screening weakens ferroelectric polarization and reduces optical anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Donor substitution offers a design lever for tuning coupled dielectric and optical properties in perovskite oxides.
method: Density functional theory for structure, energetics, and electronic properties
Density-functional perturbation theory for phonons and dielectric response
evidence_signal: Calculations indicate a dynamically stable doped structure, polar-mode hardening, reduced Born effective charges, lower static dielectric response, and an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein–Moss-type mechanism.
watch_item: Results apply only to the modeled 12.5% composition; broader doping trends and solar-cell performance are not established.
paper_title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
